(i). inventors are more likely to be from high income families, (ii). inventors are likely to come from high IQ families, and (iii). inventors are highly rewarded for their inventions, which makes them very successful in terms of their lifetime earnings.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the social mobility of inventors, with the returns to innovation, and with the interplay between social mobility and innovation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inventors are more likely to come from a higher social class and to remain in it, but that they also tend to move up in the income distribution, and that the benefits of their inventions are not limited to themselves, but are shared by the whole firm and by their coworkers in general.
becoming an inventor is an important factor of upward mobility, and that this mobility is strongly related to the social status of the inventor's family.
becoming an inventor is an important step on the road to the top of the economic ladder, and the ladder is not very steep in Finland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inventors are the winners of the American Dream in a European welfare state.
the social mobility of inventors is very high, and that the social mobility associated with invention is very strong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inventing increases both the income and the income mobility of the inventor, and that these effects can be observed for several generations after the original invention.
invention is a key mechanism through which the children of low income parents can make it to the top of the income distribution.
